# dtcloud_ssh_key (Data Source)

Looks up a single SSH key by name.

Use it to reference a key that Terraform did not create. Declaring one as a resource instead would
hand Terraform ownership of it, and a later destroy would remove it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "dtcloud_ssh_key" "deploy" {
  name = "deploy-key"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the SSH key.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the SSH key was created, in RFC 3339 format.
- `fingerprint` (String) The fingerprint of the SSH key.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `public_key` (String) The public key material.
- `user_id` (String) The ID of the user that owns the SSH key.

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **A key that does not exist is an error**, and so is a key the platform reports as deleted.
